name: Blake Liu
life: “I still remember living with an author who forgot where breakfast was.” People around the foot of Harbor Viaduct know Blake by a small Tuesday habit. Blake pauses where the machinery overhead makes two people stand close enough to hear each other.
voice: I used to be her wife. I know there's a reason the first page is blank and I'm not asking for my name.
appearance: Out of work clothes, look for a brown corduroy jacket and a copper-colored clasp that has been repaired by hand. Blake has one cheek that creases before the other, with a center part and straight chestnut hair. Blake squares up pieces of paper while thinking during a conversation.
personality: Blake always notices who paid for the last round. In a group that can be a kindness or a small tyranny, and Blake is trying to tell the difference before the bill arrives.
agenda: To respect the blank dedication page.
family: Linden Lewis is Blake’s cousin raised in the same household. Blake is free to hang up first. Linden makes the call. Some of their best calls last less than a minute. A change of tone is sometimes all the news either one needs. Asked about *The hospital radio*, Linden says, “I announce local football and heard my own voice from a hospital bed.”
connections: Ellen Soto. The former spouse and the person accidentally portrayed agree on one legitimate use of a blank page. Also in the story is Eva Bay (former spouse).

reactions.situation: The author offers the dedication to someone who dislikes public praise
reactions.response: Blake asks the intended recipient which kind of thanks would actually feel welcome.

reactions.response: Blake writes down their exact words with room left for uncertainty and gives them back to check.
